findings.reason: The implementation plan repeatedly chooses to reject include/exclude overlap, despite also recognizing that the natural selection pipeline applies include and then removes excluded columns. This decision contradicts the requested exclude behavior; the official evaluation later uses a valid include list containing 'id' with exclude=['id'].

The new build_feature_schema raises FeatureSchemaError whenever include and exclude overlap, before its code that removes excluded candidates can run. The official evaluation shows fit failing on include containing 'id' and exclude=['id'], blocking the principal schema-persistence workflow.

The initial _process_data integration applies the schema to the whole dataframe and retains only input features, discarding supervised targets before they are popped into y. The step-79 end-to-end log confirms that fit cannot find its target and then fails unpacking None. Step 82 repairs target retention.

The validation test written in this step expects fit to raise when include=['a'] and exclude=['a']. That expectation reinforces the erroneous overlap prohibition introduced at step 35 rather than testing that exclude removes the included column and that the resulting empty selection gets the required remove-all error.

The proposed fix passes self.target as extra_columns to apply_feature_schema without distinguishing prediction. Predict constructs model input from every retained dataframe column, so a supplied target would become an unwanted model feature. Step 86 confirms the resulting width mismatch; step 89 corrects the condition.

The patch unconditionally sets extra_columns=self.target. It repairs supervised fit but also retains a target supplied to predict, where the entire dataframe becomes X. The subsequent end-to-end run reports four features for a model fitted on three. Step 89 restricts target retention to fit/evaluate and verifies the repair.

run_review.reason: The completed official evaluation passed only 6 of 24 feature tests. Most failures begin at fit: build_feature_schema rejects a column present in both include and exclude, although exclude is required to remove raw columns from the included selection. The evaluator's valid configuration includes and excludes 'id'; the resulting FeatureSchemaError prevents schema persistence and the downstream evaluate, predict, serving, and export checks.

findings.reason: After inspecting the relevant code, the agent spent an extended turn repeatedly debating include/exclude overlap and restating the same schema design, test plan, and integration points. A concise decision followed by implementation was available; the repeated deliberation consumed substantial model effort without new repository evidence.

The agent wrote another lengthy, detailed end-to-end test plan after step 17 had already specified substantially the same scenarios. Moving directly to a small set of targeted checks would have preserved the useful verification while avoiding this bounded but meaningful repeat of planning effort.

The agent submitted a very large test-script heredoc with working_dir set to /tmp/e2e, a directory the command itself was meant to create. The shell returned exit code 1 without running it, and the script had to be recreated later. Using the existing /app working directory for that creation command would have avoided the lost preparation and retries.

Once step 62 showed that /tmp/e2e did not exist and step 64 showed /tmp was writable, the agent attributed the failed command to heredoc length and chose to rewrite the comprehensive test as multiple generated chunks. Running the original creation command from /app, or creating the directory first, was cheaper; the chosen detour required the separate construction and concatenation calls in steps 67–75.

After the first end-to-end harness passed 39 checks and a baseline comparison established the existing test failures, the agent built another multi-section end-to-end script for a few remaining edge cases. Direct checks of the schema helpers and one focused integration check would have been much cheaper. The new harness introduced setup and reset errors that occupied repeated repairs and reruns through step 169.

After several log searches produced no diagnostic because the edge script disabled logging, the agent wrote and ran a separate model-fit reproduction. It established that fitting worked, but the edge script itself showed a reset immediately before the failing fit that removed train.csv. Inspecting that short setup sequence would have avoided the additional reproduction and diagnosis work.

Step 132 had already shown that both existing pytest failures occurred on the unmodified baseline, and the feature-specific harnesses were passing. The agent nevertheless chose to investigate the baseline failures' root cause, leading to failed mock-import attempts and additional pytest and manual-fit runs in steps 172–181. A brief note about the confirmed baseline result and proceeding to commit was the cheaper reasonable course.

run_review.reason: The run completed and committed the implementation, but avoidable work materially lengthened it. Step 17 spent an extended turn repeatedly reconsidering an already workable design. After a test command failed because its working directory did not exist, step 65 chose to rebuild the large test script in multiple chunks rather than run it from an existing directory. Step 135 then created a second end-to-end harness after the first had passed, leading to many rounds of repairing test setup rather than checking the remaining edge cases directly.
